hero.headline: US Employers Add 57,000 Jobs in June as Hiring Slows Sharply
hero.body:
US employers added 57,000 jobs in June, falling well short of economist expectations and marking a sharp deceleration in hiring. The figure represents roughly half the number that forecasters had predicted, signaling weakness in the labor market. The Bureau of Labor Statistics also revised employment figures downward for the previous two months by a combined total of 74,000 jobs, with May figures reduced from 172,000 to 129,000 and April figures lowered from 179,000 to 148,000.

Despite sluggish job creation, the unemployment rate edged down to 4.2%. However, this decline reflects labor force attrition rather than robust hiring. Approximately 720,000 people left the labor force during the month, which helped lower the jobless rate even as the total number of unemployed people remained relatively stable.

Private employers added 98,000 jobs according to payroll data from ADP. Pay growth for workers who remained in their jobs throughout the year increased 4.4% compared to the prior year, with the finance sector leading at 5% annual growth.

The healthcare industry, which has been a primary driver of recent job gains, added 22,000 positions in June but at a notably slower pace than its monthly average of 38,000. The hospitality and leisure sector unexpectedly declined by 61,000 jobs, a weakness that surprised analysts given the World Cup soccer matches hosted across the country during the month.

Over the past three months, employers have added an average of about 111,000 jobs monthly, a figure that remains substantially higher than the sluggish growth experienced in the fall and winter. However, the broader trend suggests the post-pandemic hiring surge has cooled considerably.

Dr Nela Richardson, chief economist at ADP, characterized the current environment as reflecting both supply and demand constraints. "We know it's taking people longer to find work, but there also are signs of labor supply constraints in certain industries," she said, adding that the overall effect is a slowdown in job creation.

The report carries implications for Federal Reserve policy decisions. The weaker employment data reduces pressure on the central bank to raise interest rates, as slower hiring suggests diminished wage growth pressures. The Fed has held interest rates steady since December but indicated in June projections that most members expect at least one rate increase before year's end.

Financial markets showed mixed reactions to the employment figures. While weaker hiring data suggested the Fed might pause further rate increases, investors also contended with persistent inflation concerns. The June inflation report is expected later this month, with prices at the pump remaining elevated due to Middle East tensions.

The combination of minimal job creation and declining workforce participation raises questions about the sustainability of recent economic improvements as the labor market enters a more cautious phase.

cards.headline: Russian Strike on Kyiv Kills at Least 27 in Largest Assault on Capital
cards.body:
Russia launched one of its most extensive attacks on Kyiv, killing at least 27 people in what officials described as the deadliest night raid on the Ukrainian capital in recent months. The overnight bombardment deployed the largest number of weapons yet used against the city, striking more than 20 locations across residential and infrastructure targets.

Ukrainian air force data showed that Russia fired 629 missiles and drones in the assault, including 11 ballistic missiles, 20 cruise missiles, and 598 Shahed drones. Air defense systems intercepted or jammed a large proportion of the incoming weapons, including 563 of the drones, but several high-speed ballistic missiles and cruise missiles struck their targets.

The heaviest toll came when a five-story residential building in the eastern Darnytskyi district was hit in the middle of the night, killing 17 people including at least four children. Rescue services said 10 more people were missing from the building, though not all may have been inside at the time. Another person died in a separate strike near Kyiv's central railway station, where attacks damaged buildings housing offices of the EU delegation to Ukraine and the British Council. Both organizations confirmed their offices sustained severe damage.

Waves of explosions shook the capital starting after 3am and continuing after 5:30am. Damage was recorded at around 30 locations throughout the city, with most being ordinary residential buildings. A railway siding in eastern Kyiv was also hit, leaving some intercity train carriages burned out. A total of 38 people were wounded in the attacks.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy had previously warned that Moscow was preparing a major strike in response to Ukrainian forces hitting targets inside Russian territory. He said the bombardment demonstrated Russia's rejection of peace efforts. "These Russian missiles and attack drones today are a clear response to everyone in the world who has been calling for a ceasefire and for real diplomacy," Zelenskyy said on social media.

The assault marked a return to intensive bombing of Kyiv after a relatively quieter August period. Kyiv's mayor Vitali Klitschko called it a barbaric attack and declared Friday a day of mourning for the capital.

Zelenskyy called for an international response, including further sanctions against Russia. He specifically appealed to China, Russia's ally, to respond to the strikes. The Kremlin said it remained interested in diplomacy but would continue launching strikes on Ukraine.

The attack represents a significant escalation in the conflict, with both sides demonstrating willingness to strike deeper into enemy territory and target civilian areas.

cards.headline: US and Iran Hold Talks in Qatar, Agree to Continue Discussions
cards.teaser: Negotiations paused for a slain ayatollah's funeral after both sides and mediators reported progress.
cards.body:
U.S. and Iranian negotiators met separately in Qatar on Wednesday with Qatari and Pakistani mediators present. Both sides reported positive progress from the discussions and agreed to continue their talks.

The negotiations were scheduled to pause temporarily to allow for the funeral of a senior Iranian ayatollah. The separate meeting format represents an ongoing diplomatic channel between the two countries on regional matters.

cards.headline: Dangerous heat wave grips US ahead of Fourth of July weekend
cards.body:
A severe heat wave is sweeping across the central and eastern United States, bringing dangerous conditions just as Americans prepare for Independence Day celebrations. The National Weather Service has warned of record-breaking temperatures combined with high humidity that will create hazardous heat index values across the region.

Temperatures between 95F and 105F, combined with high humidity, are pushing heat index values to between 100F and 115F across much of the affected area. The National Weather Service stated this will create "widespread areas of major to extreme heat risk from the Midwest to the East Coast," with numerous daily temperature records expected through Friday and Independence Day itself. Some areas may see consecutive-day, monthly, and all-time records broken.

The extreme heat is expected to continue across most of the central and eastern US through Friday, then shift focus to the eastern US through the Independence Day weekend. Peak heat indices could reach as high as 115 degrees in some locations.

The agency emphasized that "prolonged periods of extreme heat are among the deadliest weather hazards" in the country because impacts accumulate over time. Officials urged residents to limit time outdoors, stay hydrated, and ensure access to air conditioning or cooling centers.

In New York City, temperatures reached 100F in Central Park on Thursday afternoon, marking the park's first triple-digit day since July 2012. Forecasters warned of dangerous heat and humidity through Saturday, with heat index values potentially reaching 115F. New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani urged residents to prepare, stating "Please stay prepared and informed as these dangerously high temperatures continue." He announced that the city was deploying cooling vans staffed with medical personnel who would provide wellness checks, medical care, water, electrolytes, and sunscreen, along with transport to cooling centers.

New York Governor Kathy Hochul warned that the state's electric grid was under heavy strain from increased energy demand. She encouraged residents to voluntarily conserve power by setting air conditioning between 75F and 78F and avoiding unnecessary appliance use.

Across the region, additional impacts emerged. Philadelphia experienced temperatures of 102F on Thursday, and organizers of the city's Independence Day parade shortened the route due to the extreme heat. The mid-Atlantic region faced warnings of heat indices up to 110F, with possible severe thunderstorms adding to dangerous conditions.

Washington DC Mayor Muriel Bowser urged residents to factor the extreme temperatures into their Fourth of July plans, advising people to avoid strenuous outdoor activity, drink plenty of water, wear sunscreen, and limit time outdoors whenever possible.

The dangerous conditions extend across Kentucky, Missouri, Illinois, and Indiana, where heat index values could reach 110F.

cards.headline: Nasdaq Falls After June Jobs Report Misses Expectations
cards.teaser: Stock markets posted mixed results Thursday as investors digested weaker-than-expected June employment data.
cards.body:
The Nasdaq declined as technology and chip stocks faced continued pressure following June's weaker-than-expected jobs report. By contrast, the Dow Jones Industrial Average climbed more than 200 points to reach a record high, reflecting divergent performance across market sectors.

The June employment data showed employers added fewer jobs than in May, though the unemployment rate edged lower. Market participants debated the implications for Federal Reserve interest rate policy, with some interpreting softer hiring as reducing the chance of further rate increases, while others viewed it as a potential warning sign for economic growth.

cards.headline: Trump administration cancels teen pregnancy prevention grants
cards.teaser: The Department of Health and Human Services canceled tens of millions of dollars in teen pregnancy prevention grants, prompting Democrats to demand reinstatement.
cards.body:
Democrats in both the House and Senate are demanding the Trump administration restore teen pregnancy prevention grants that were abruptly canceled last week. The Department of Health and Human Services terminated the funding without notifying program recipients in advance.

In the House, 79 Democrats led by members of the Democratic Women's Caucus sent a letter to Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy calling for reinstatement of the grants. The canceled funding had supported programs nationwide aimed at reducing teen pregnancy rates.

cards.headline: Top Army general in Europe and Africa steps down after ouster
cards.teaser: Army Gen. Christopher Donahue relinquished command in Germany after Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth unexpectedly removed him from the position last month.
cards.body:
Army Gen. Christopher Donahue formally relinquished command of U.S. Army Europe and Africa at a ceremony in Wiesbaden, Germany. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth removed Donahue from the position last month in a move that surprised military observers.

Donahue, 56, spent decades in military special operations and was considered a rising star in the Army. His removal by Hegseth was unexpected given his reputation and career trajectory within the service.

cards.headline: Pope Leo XIV Excommunicates Society of St. Pius X in First Major Crisis of Papacy
cards.teaser: The Vatican took action against the traditionalist group after it consecrated bishops in defiance of papal authority.
cards.body:
The Vatican declared the Society of St. Pius X in schism and excommunicated its bishops and priests after the group consecrated new bishops without papal consent. The move represents a significant challenge early in Pope Leo XIV's papacy.

The Society of St. Pius X has long clashed with the Church over theological and liturgical matters, rejecting reforms from the Second Vatican Council and maintaining traditional Latin Mass practices. The unauthorized episcopal consecrations triggered the formal excommunication response from Rome.

cards.headline: Germany Charges Ukrainian National Over Nord Stream Pipeline Explosions
cards.teaser: German prosecutors accused Ukraine of ordering the 2022 sabotage that destroyed sections of the gas pipelines.
cards.body:
German prosecutors have charged a Ukrainian national in connection with the 2022 Nord Stream pipeline explosions, alleging the suspect was directed by Ukrainian state authorities. The underwater gas pipelines connecting Russia to Germany were nearly destroyed in the sabotage attack in the Baltic Sea, severing a major energy supply route to Europe.

Ukraine has denied involvement in the case. The charges are likely to create tensions between Kyiv and Germany, which has been its largest military supporter since Russia's invasion.

cards.headline: Truck Crash Kills 9 Buddhist Monks on Pilgrimage in Thailand
cards.teaser: A boy driving a pickup truck struck a religious procession in the northeast, injuring 11 others.
cards.body:
An 11-year-old boy drove his parents' truck into a Buddhist procession in Mukdahan, northeast Thailand, killing at least nine monks. The monks were walking in their orange robes as part of a religious pilgrimage when the vehicle struck the group. CCTV footage captured the moment of impact on the roadway shortly before 11am local time on Thursday.

Eleven other monks sustained injuries in the collision. Police are still establishing the circumstances of the incident, and charges have yet to be filed against the boy.

cards.headline: Two Killers Sentenced to Life for Murder of British Couple in South Africa
cards.teaser: The pair had been collecting rare plants and seeds before their bodies were discovered in a river.
cards.body:
A South African court has sentenced two individuals to life imprisonment for the murder of a British couple. The victims were collecting rare plants and seeds in the country as part of their botanical work when they were killed. Their bodies were discovered in a river several days after they went missing during their expedition.

The court imposed the maximum sentence following the murder convictions of the two defendants.

cards.headline: US and Iran Hold Talks in Qatar, Agree to Continue Discussions
cards.teaser: Negotiations paused for a slain ayatollah's funeral after both sides and mediators reported progress.
cards.body:
U.S. and Iranian negotiators met separately in Qatar on Wednesday with Qatari and Pakistani mediators present. Both sides reported positive progress from the discussions and agreed to continue their talks.

The negotiations were scheduled to pause temporarily to allow for the funeral of a senior Iranian ayatollah. The separate meeting format represents an ongoing diplomatic channel between the two countries on regional matters.

cards.headline: Vietnam's Economic Growth Masks Deep Frustrations Despite High Exports
cards.teaser: The country posts strong GDP figures and trade numbers while citizens express discontent.
cards.body:
Vietnam has recorded high economic growth rates and surging exports, establishing itself as one of Asia's most ambitious economies. The country has attracted significant foreign investment and built massive infrastructure projects, including the world's largest stadium. Official statistics show Vietnam's economy expanding rapidly.

Despite the positive macroeconomic indicators, deep frustrations persist among Vietnamese citizens. The disconnect between national growth figures and individual economic experiences has created tension in the country. Observers note that headline economic success has not translated into widespread prosperity or addressed underlying social and economic challenges facing ordinary Vietnamese.

cards.headline: Ocasio-Cortez backs El-Sayed in Michigan Democratic Senate primary
cards.teaser: Representative Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez endorsed Abdul El-Sayed in Michigan's Democratic Senate primary race.
cards.body:
Representative Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez has endorsed Abdul El-Sayed in Michigan's Democratic Senate primary. El-Sayed, a doctor and former public health director, is backed by Senator Bernie Sanders and currently leads in polls ahead of other candidates including Haley Stevens and Mallory McMorrow.

In an interview with the New York Times, Ocasio-Cortez expressed her support for El-Sayed despite acknowledging ideological differences within the party. "Every single one of us sees this moment as existential," she said. The endorsement underscores the ongoing split between the party's progressive and establishment factions in this closely watched race.

cards.headline: Former Olympic canoeist faces felony charge over incident at Reflecting Pool
cards.teaser: A former Olympian was indicted on a felony charge following an arrest at the Reflecting Pool in Washington.
cards.body:
A former Olympic canoeist has been indicted by a grand jury on a felony charge after an incident at the Reflecting Pool in Washington. The athlete was arrested after allegedly reaching into the Reflecting Pool, according to the US attorney for the District of Columbia.

The charge represents an escalation from the initial arrest. The Reflecting Pool, located on the National Mall, is a prominent memorial site. The case has drawn attention given the athlete's Olympic background and the nature of the alleged vandalism at the national landmark.

cards.headline: Congressional report says Trump redirected 250th anniversary funds for political purposes
cards.teaser: A House Democratic report alleges that fundraising for America's 250th anniversary was hijacked to serve political ideology and personal projects.
cards.body:
House Democrats released a congressional report accusing former President Trump of hijacking the nation's 250th anniversary celebration for political gain. According to the investigation, Trump and his allies redirected the commemorative effort to enrich political associates, harvest voter data, and promote Christian nationalist ideology. The report, titled "From Vanity to Insanity: How the White House Cheated the American People Out of Their 250th Birthday," documents alleged corruption, wire fraud, and pay-to-play schemes.

The investigation centers on a shadow corporation embedded within the National Park Foundation that organized aspects of the anniversary planning. Donors to the Trump-backed Freedom 250 organization were allegedly misled about how their contributions would be used, raising questions about fees charged by firms run by Trump allies managing the 250th anniversary events.

cards.headline: England advances to T20 World Cup final with win over South Africa
cards.teaser: England defeated South Africa by 40 runs at The Oval to reach the T20 World Cup final.
cards.body:
England secured a place in the T20 World Cup final with a dominant 40-run victory over South Africa at The Oval. Sciver-Brunt delivered a superb performance to lead the team to victory in the semi-final.

England will face Australia in Sunday's final after the hosts cruised into the championship match. The comprehensive win demonstrates the team's strong form heading into the tournament's decisive match.

cards.headline: UK extends pub hours to 5am for England-Mexico World Cup match
cards.teaser: The British government reversed its earlier stance and will allow pubs to remain open until 5am for the England-Mexico match.
cards.body:
Pubs across the UK will be allowed to stay open until 5am for the England-Mexico World Cup match, marking a reversal of the government's earlier stance on relaxing licensing laws for the tournament. The fixture kicks off at 1am British Summer Time on Monday.

England manager Thomas Tuchel has encouraged young fans to stay up for the crucial match. However, the early kickoff time has sparked discussion about whether children should watch live or wait for spoiler-free recaps the following day.

cards.headline: Pope excommunicates Society of St. Pius X
cards.teaser: Pope Leo excommunicated the Society of St. Pius X, a traditionalist Catholic group, for ordaining bishops without papal permission.
cards.body:
The Vatican declared the Society of St. Pius X in schism and excommunicated its bishops and priests after the traditionalist group consecrated bishops without papal consent. This unauthorized ordination served as the immediate trigger for the church's formal response.

The conflict between the Society and Rome extends well beyond this single incident. The organization has long resisted reforms implemented by the modern Catholic Church, maintaining theological and liturgical positions at odds with Vatican doctrine. This fundamental disagreement has kept the group separated from full communion with the church for an extended period.

cards.headline: Tesla Deliveries Hit Record Despite Stock Decline
cards.teaser: Tesla reported record quarterly vehicle deliveries driven by a recovery in European sales, though its stock fell 8 percent.
cards.body:
Tesla achieved record quarterly deliveries with a 3 percent increase in overall vehicle sales and a 25 percent surge in Europe. The strong European performance fueled optimism about the company's ability to achieve annual growth despite a slowdown in global car sales.

Despite the delivery milestone, Tesla's stock fell 8 percent. The divergence between operational performance and market reaction suggests investors either anticipated the strong results or hold concerns about future demand and Tesla's competitive standing in the electric vehicle market.

cards.headline: Trump Discloses 327 Unreported Stock Trades Made Day Before Tariff Pause
cards.teaser: President Trump disclosed 327 previously unreported stock trades made one day before he announced a reversal on tariffs.
cards.body:
President Trump's financial disclosure revealed 327 previously unreported stock trades executed a day before announcing a tariff pause that triggered a market rebound. The trades included purchases of major technology companies such as Apple and Nvidia, which benefited significantly from the subsequent policy reversal.

Financial filings show Trump earned more than $2 billion in 2025, with over $1 billion coming from cryptocurrency ventures—an industry he has actively sought to deregulate. The president's earnings from crypto substantially exceeded his income from real estate and Trump-branded merchandise.

cards.headline: Ford Sales Drop 10 Percent in Second Quarter
cards.teaser: Ford reported a 10 percent decline in second quarter sales as the company underwent business transformation.
cards.body:
Ford's second quarter sales declined 10.3 percent year-over-year, weighed down by supplier constraints affecting F-Series trucks, reduced electric vehicle demand, and a smaller rental business. The company also discontinued certain models including the Escape.

The quarter showed mixed results across Ford's lineup. The Bronco and Maverick hybrid achieved sales records, while large SUVs and remaining F-Series inventory drove growth in the first half of 2026. The sales drop reflects broader industry challenges as automakers transition toward electric vehicles and respond to changing consumer demand.

cards.headline: Meta Stock Drops as Company Announces Cloud Computing Push
cards.teaser: Meta's stock fell after the company revealed plans to sell excess artificial intelligence computing capacity as a cloud service.
cards.body:
Meta is building a cloud business to sell excess AI computing capacity, according to Bloomberg News. This move puts the company in competition with Amazon Web Services, Microsoft Azure, and Google Cloud as it looks to monetize its AI infrastructure investments.

Wall Street responded negatively to the announcement. Analysts cautioned that cloud services typically operate with lower profit margins than Meta's core advertising business, prompting the stock decline.

cards.headline: Data Centers Ordered to Use Backup Power Amid Heat Wave
cards.teaser: The Trump administration directed grid managers to require data centers to use backup power as triple-digit temperatures strain electrical grids.
cards.body:
The Trump administration instructed electrical grid managers to require data centers to switch to backup power sources as extreme heat engulfs much of the United States. The directive aims to reduce strain on power grids struggling to meet demand during the heat wave, which has brought triple-digit temperatures to large portions of the country. Data centers typically maintain backup power systems that often go unused during normal operations.

The order represents a rare intervention in energy infrastructure management to prevent potential blackouts. Data centers consume enormous amounts of electricity to power servers and cooling systems, making them significant contributors to grid demand. By shifting these facilities to backup power during peak usage periods, grid operators hope to preserve capacity for residential and other critical uses during the dangerous heat wave.

hero.headline: IQM becomes Europe's first public quantum computing company despite uncertain future
hero.body:
IQM, a quantum computing company based in Finland, began trading on the Nasdaq today with a valuation of approximately $1.9 billion, becoming the first European quantum company to go public. The company describes itself as a full-stack quantum operation, meaning it handles both hardware and software development for quantum computing systems.

The public debut comes with an acknowledgment from IQM itself that the future of quantum technology remains uncertain. This candid admission reflects the broader reality facing the quantum computing industry, which has attracted substantial investment despite the technology still being in relatively early stages of development. Quantum computers use the principles of quantum mechanics to process information in ways that could eventually solve certain problems much faster than traditional computers.

The $1.9 billion valuation places significant market expectations on IQM to deliver on the promises of quantum computing. The company joins a small group of quantum computing firms that have accessed public markets, though most remain private as they continue to develop commercially viable applications. The quantum computing sector has seen waves of enthusiasm and skepticism as companies work to move beyond laboratory demonstrations to practical, revenue-generating systems.

IQM's willingness to publicly state uncertainty about the technology's future sets it apart from some competitors who have made bolder claims about quantum computing timelines. The quantum industry has faced criticism for overpromising on near-term capabilities, and investors have begun demanding more realistic assessments of when quantum computers might solve real-world problems that justify their development costs.

The company's public listing provides it with capital to continue research and development, but also subjects it to quarterly reporting requirements and shareholder scrutiny. IQM will need to balance the long-term nature of quantum technology development with the expectations of public market investors seeking evidence of progress and eventual profitability.

cards.headline: FAA proposes allowing supersonic flights over US cities if aircraft meet noise limits
cards.teaser: New federal rules would permit supersonic commercial flights over land if the aircraft produce minimal sonic booms.
cards.body:
The Federal Aviation Administration has proposed new regulations that would legalize supersonic flight over United States cities, ending a decades-long ban on such operations. The key condition is that aircraft must be quiet enough to avoid producing the loud sonic booms that previously made overland supersonic travel unacceptable.

The proposal represents a shift in aviation policy that could enable a new generation of supersonic airliners. Current regulations prohibit supersonic flight over land due to noise concerns, a rule that has been in place since the era of the Concorde. The proposed changes would clear a regulatory path for companies developing quieter supersonic aircraft to operate domestic routes.

cards.headline: Anthropic in talks with Samsung to develop custom AI chip
cards.teaser: The AI company is exploring a partnership with the electronics manufacturer for specialized processors.
cards.body:
Anthropic is in discussions with Samsung about creating a custom artificial intelligence chip tailored to the company's needs. This potential partnership would provide Anthropic with specialized hardware optimized for its AI systems.

The announcement comes roughly a week after OpenAI revealed its own custom chip initiative through a partnership with Broadcom, highlighting a competitive race among leading AI firms to secure dedicated hardware and refine chip architectures for their specific applications.

cards.headline: Meta launches Pocket app for AI-generated mini games
cards.teaser: The experimental application lets users create and share interactive games using text prompts.
cards.body:
Meta has quietly launched Pocket, an experimental AI app that enables users to generate and share interactive mini games through text prompts. The app leverages natural language processing to transform user descriptions into playable games that can be shared across the platform.

The release reflects Meta's ongoing investment in AI-powered creative tools and gaming experiences. Rather than a high-profile announcement, the company opted for a quiet launch strategy for this experimental offering.

cards.headline: Travel app Hopper to pay $35 million in FTC settlement over hidden fees
cards.teaser: The Federal Trade Commission says the company used deceptive practices to mislead travelers about service costs.
cards.body:
Hopper will pay $35 million to settle Federal Trade Commission allegations that it used deceptive "dark patterns" to hide fees and mislead customers about service costs and benefits. Dark patterns are interface designs that manipulate users into making decisions they might not otherwise make.

The settlement is part of the FTC's broader enforcement efforts against companies that use confusing pricing displays or pressure tactics to extract additional fees from consumers.

cards.headline: Scientists discover planet orbiting dead star, offering preview of solar system's fate
cards.teaser: The James Webb Space Telescope observed a planet that survived its star's death, showing what may await Earth.
cards.body:
Astronomers have detected a planet orbiting a white dwarf star using the James Webb Space Telescope. The discovery reveals that planets can survive the dramatic final stages of stellar death. White dwarfs are stellar remnants left behind after stars like our sun burn through their fuel and expel their outer layers.

The research team identified aerosols and hydrocarbons in the planet's atmosphere, according to findings published in Nature. The observation demonstrates that a star's death does not necessarily doom all planets in its orbit, offering a glimpse into what may eventually happen to planets in our own solar system.

cards.headline: New macOS malware uses advanced techniques to avoid detection
cards.teaser: PamStealer employs sophisticated methods to remain hidden on infected Mac computers.
cards.body:
Security researchers have identified a new strain of macOS malware called PamStealer that uses advanced tradecraft to evade detection. The malware represents an escalation in sophistication for threats targeting Apple computers.

PamStealer's stealthy capabilities make it more difficult for traditional security software to identify and remove compared to earlier Mac malware. The discovery highlights ongoing efforts by malware developers to find ways around macOS security protections.

hero.headline: Jaylen Brown traded from Celtics to 76ers
hero.body:
The Boston Celtics have traded 2024 NBA Finals MVP Jaylen Brown to the Philadelphia 76ers in a significant offseason move that reshapes both franchises. The Celtics will receive Paul George and substantial draft capital in return, including two first-round picks and two second-round selections.

Brown, who led the Celtics to victory in the 2024 NBA Finals, addressed the trade publicly, expressing mixed emotions about the move. He said he is both excited and disappointed about leaving Boston for Philadelphia.

The trade comes after what reports describe as a stormy few weeks, during which Brown had grown unhappy with his treatment by the Celtics organization. His departure marks the end of a significant era in Boston, where he had established himself as one of the league's premier two-way players and a cornerstone of the franchise's recent success.

The 76ers are making an aggressive move during free agency, signaling their intention to compete immediately for a championship in the Eastern Conference. By acquiring Brown, one of the NBA's top perimeter defenders and scorers, Philadelphia is fundamentally reshaping its roster and adding star power to their lineup.

The addition of Paul George to Boston represents a notable shift in the team's direction following Brown's departure. George brings championship experience and additional scoring ability to the Celtics as they recalibrate after losing one of their star players.

This trade is part of a busy offseason across the NBA, with multiple teams making significant roster moves. Both the Celtics and 76ers are taking bold steps to reshape their competitive positioning in the Eastern Conference, one of the league's most challenging divisions.

Brown's mixed emotions about the trade underscore the complexity of the move. While leaving a franchise where he had deep roots and achieved considerable success is difficult, the opportunity to join a 76ers team actively pursuing a championship provides new motivation and direction for his career.

The trade represents one of the most substantial moves of the offseason, involving multiple draft picks and two established NBA stars. As teams continue to make moves during free agency, this blockbuster deal demonstrates the lengths franchises will go to in pursuit of championship rosters.

Both organizations will now focus on integrating their new players and building cohesive rosters capable of competing for titles. The Celtics will work to establish chemistry with George while adjusting to life without Brown, while Philadelphia aims to build a championship-contending team around their newly acquired star.

cards.headline: Caitlin Clark named WNBA All-Star starter for third straight year
cards.teaser: Clark will start the All-Star Game alongside Fever teammates Kelsey Mitchell and Aliyah Boston.
cards.body:
Caitlin Clark has been voted to start in her third consecutive WNBA All-Star Game. The Indiana Fever guard will be joined in the starting lineup by teammates Kelsey Mitchell and Aliyah Boston.

The selection marks a significant achievement for both Clark and the Fever franchise, with three players from the same team earning All-Star starter spots through fan voting.

cards.headline: 76ers sign Anfernee Simons to two-year deal
cards.teaser: The free agent guard agreed to a $12.3 million contract with a player option for the second season.
cards.body:
Free agent guard Anfernee Simons has signed a two-year, $12.3 million contract with the Philadelphia 76ers. The deal includes a player option for the second season, allowing Simons flexibility moving forward.

The signing is part of Philadelphia's significant offseason roster overhaul as the team reshapes its backcourt.

cards.headline: NBA to test one free throw rule in summer league
cards.teaser: The league will experiment with the rule previously tested in the G League during July's summer league games.
cards.body:
The NBA summer league will test a one free throw rule during July's series. This experimental format has already been used in the G League and is being evaluated as a potential regular season change.

The league will also embed sensors in basketballs during the summer league. These tests will help the NBA gather data on innovations before deciding whether to implement them during official play.

cards.headline: Rays overtake Yankees atop MLB power rankings
cards.teaser: Tampa Bay moved into the top spot in the American League while Miami cracked the top 10.
cards.body:
The Tampa Bay Rays have knocked the New York Yankees out of the top spot in the American League in Week 14 power rankings. Tampa Bay's strong performance has vaulted the team to the top of the AL standings as the season approaches its midpoint.

The Miami Marlins also made significant movement, cracking the top 10 in the rankings. The strong showing from both Florida teams represents a surge for baseball in the state as both franchises trend upward heading into the second half of the season.

cards.headline: Djokovic defends Serena Williams after Wimbledon loss
cards.teaser: The men's tennis star called for less criticism of Williams following her singles return.
cards.body:
Novak Djokovic has called for people to "cool off a little bit" regarding criticism of Serena Williams following her loss in singles competition at Wimbledon this week. The men's tennis star publicly defended Williams as she returned to the tour after time away.

Djokovic's comments suggest the scrutiny Williams faced after her defeat was excessive, urging observers to show more restraint in their responses to her performance at the tournament.

cards.headline: Trade speculation surrounds Skubal, Arraez, Peralta ahead of deadline
cards.teaser: Multiple top players could change teams before the trade deadline one month away.
cards.body:
With the trade deadline one month away, Tarik Skubal, Luis Arraez, and Freddy Peralta are among the players being discussed as potential trade candidates.

The deadline typically prompts significant roster movement as contending teams strengthen their lineups for playoff runs while rebuilding teams seek prospects.

hero.headline: Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce Wedding Set for Friday at Madison Square Garden
hero.body:
Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce are preparing to celebrate their wedding at Madison Square Garden this Friday, according to permit documents obtained by the Associated Press. The high-profile event is expected to draw approximately 1,000 guests and will span multiple days of celebrations in New York City.

The couple has confirmed a substantial charitable contribution ahead of the festivities. Swift and Kelce donated $26 million to 20 charities across the United States, with organizations selected from cities meaningful to both of them. The beneficiaries include food banks and community organizations in Nashville, Kansas City, New York City, and other locations. While the couple has not explicitly connected the donations to the wedding, the timing and choice of charities suggest a link to the celebration.

According to the permit documents, the festivities begin Thursday evening with a pre-party celebration expected to start at 6:30 p.m., likely serving as a rehearsal dinner. The main event is scheduled to run Friday from 5 p.m. until 4 a.m. Saturday. The permit application extends through midday Saturday to allow for cleanup and street closure management.

The venue choice reflects the scale and security requirements of hosting such a significant event. Madison Square Garden can accommodate large gatherings while providing the privacy controls and security measures difficult to achieve at traditional wedding venues. The permit process required street closures around the arena, with multiple entrance and drive-through tents to be erected for guest arrivals.

Swift previously discussed her wedding plans during an appearance on The Graham Norton show, describing it as "huge" and emphasizing that the celebration would be designed to be enjoyable rather than stressful. She indicated the large guest list would allow for a fun planning process without the complications that come with smaller, more restrictive affairs.

Visible preparations around the arena on Thursday included food deliveries from various suppliers, indicating substantial catering operations underway. The complex logistics of hosting such an event at an arena typically used for concerts and sports events have required extensive coordination with city officials and vendors.

The couple has maintained privacy regarding specific wedding details, though they have not denied reports about the event. Entertainment observers have described the celebration as potentially the most significant celebrity wedding of the decade, given Swift's global fanbase and Kelce's prominence in professional football. The gathering occurs amid a heatwave affecting New York City and during America's 250th anniversary celebrations.

While fans and media outlets have speculated extensively about the guest list and logistics, the couple has controlled information through reported nondisclosure agreements with invitees. The combination of Swift's established practice of generous gestures toward collaborators and crew, along with the charitable donations and confirmed permits, has solidified expectations that the wedding celebration will proceed this weekend.

cards.headline: Seth Rogen Says Anne Hathaway Left Knocked Up Over Birthing Scene
cards.teaser: The actor recalled on a podcast that Hathaway quit the 2007 comedy after concerns about a graphic scene did not align with her brand.
cards.body:
Seth Rogen revealed on The A24 Podcast that Anne Hathaway withdrew from Knocked Up because she objected to a graphic birthing scene in the film. Rogen explained that Hathaway felt the scene didn't align with her public image.

Rogen appeared on the podcast alongside director and co-star Olivia Wilde. Katherine Heigl ultimately took on the female lead role opposite Rogen in Judd Apatow's 2007 comedy, which became a box office success.

cards.headline: John Oliver Makes Armed Entrance on General Hospital
cards.teaser: The HBO host appeared in the daytime soap opera arriving by helicopter with armed guards in a dark suit and jet black hair.
cards.body:
John Oliver made a dramatic appearance on General Hospital in an episode that aired Thursday. The HBO host descended from a helicopter flanked by armed guards, wearing a dark suit and sporting jet black hair as he surveyed the aftermath of events in Port Charles, New York.

A co-star described Oliver's performance as incredible. The cameo appearance marks an unusual crossover between late-night comedy and daytime television. General Hospital is a long-running ABC soap opera set in the fictional town of Port Charles.

cards.headline: Midjourney Demands Studios Disclose AI Use in Copyright Case
cards.teaser: The AI image lab is trying to force Disney, Universal, and Warner Bros. to reveal their artificial intelligence practices as it defends against a copyright lawsuit.
cards.body:
Midjourney is seeking to force Disney, Universal, and Warner Bros. to reveal how they use artificial intelligence in their own operations as part of its defense against a copyright lawsuit. The studios sued the AI image generator last year, claiming it facilitated widespread infringement of their copyrighted characters.

The company is relying on a fair use defense in the case, which carries potentially significant financial stakes. The studios' lawsuit accuses Midjourney of enabling massive copyright violations involving their intellectual property.

cards.headline: A Capitol Fourth Rehearsal Closed to Public Due to Heat
cards.teaser: The rehearsal for the Independence Day concert was canceled for public attendance because of high temperatures in Washington.
cards.body:
The rehearsal for A Capitol Fourth concert was closed to the public Thursday because of heat conditions in Washington. The annual Independence Day celebration concert is scheduled to air on PBS and typically draws large crowds to the U.S. Capitol grounds.

Broadway performers are set to appear at the concert, which celebrates American independence. Reports indicate that heat conditions have raised concerns about the main event itself, though organizers have not announced a cancellation of the Friday concert. The special typically features musical performances and patriotic programming.

cards.headline: Questlove Launches Talk Show Built Around Celebrity Game Night
cards.teaser: The Roots drummer created The Next Move, a program where guests play Uno, Jenga, and other games while talking.
cards.body:
Questlove has added talk show host to his roles with the launch of The Next Move. The Roots drummer designed the program around a celebrity game night format where guests play board games and card games including Uno and Jenga while having conversations.

The format represents a departure from traditional talk show structures. Questlove has built a career spanning music, film, and television production. The new show adds another project to his portfolio of entertainment work.

cards.headline: Hollywood Figures Launch New Artist Funding Initiative Harbor Fund
cards.teaser: Chris Pine and other entertainment industry figures have created a funding source they hope will support artistic projects similar to Impact Partners.
cards.body:
A group of Hollywood figures including Chris Pine has established Harbor Fund, a new initiative designed to provide funding for artists and their projects. The organizers hope the fund will serve a role similar to Impact Partners and Artemis Rising Foundation, which have supported documentary filmmakers for more than two decades.

The fund represents the latest example of wealthy individuals supporting artistic work, a practice with historical precedents including the Medici family's patronage of Leonardo da Vinci and Michelangelo, and Peggy Guggenheim's support of Jackson Pollock. The entertainment industry backers aim to create a sustainable funding source for creative projects.

hero.headline: House Republicans clash over voter ID bill as lawmaker blocks floor action
hero.body:
House Republicans Pass $70 Billion Immigration Funding Bill

House Republicans approved a $70 billion spending measure on Tuesday that funds immigration enforcement agencies through the end of Donald Trump's presidential term, resolving a months-long dispute with Democrats that had previously forced a government shutdown.

The Secure America Act passed 214-212, largely along party lines, with only one Republican-aligned independent and all Democrats voting against it. The Senate had approved the bill the previous week. It allocates $38 billion to Immigration and Customs Enforcement, $26 billion to Customs and Border Protection, and $5 billion to the Department of Homeland Security through September 2029. The bill now awaits Trump's signature.

House Speaker Mike Johnson framed the passage as a Republican victory, stating: "With today's vote, House and Senate Republicans have officially ended the third Democrat government shutdown of this Congress." He argued that Democrats had achieved nothing through their shutdown strategy and suggested it demonstrated voter rejection of Democratic immigration policies.

The legislation ends a funding blockade that Democrats initiated in January following the deaths of two US citizens killed by federal agents during an immigration enforcement operation in Minneapolis. The Democratic boycott forced the Department of Homeland Security to shut down for 75 days beginning in mid-February. The agency reopened in late April after Democrats agreed to fund all DHS operations except the two immigration enforcement agencies. Republicans then moved to secure permanent funding for ICE and CBP, arguing it would prevent future Democratic shutdowns.

House Democrats unanimously opposed the bill. Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries called it a "blank check to ICE without any guardrails, any oversight, any accountability." Republicans countered these criticisms by accusing Democrats of attempting to undermine law enforcement. House Majority Leader Steve Scalise stated: "You vote no, you are voting to defund the police. Those are the people, the law enforcement officers, risking their lives to keep our community safe."

The bill's passage represents an achievement for Johnson, who leads a historically narrow Republican majority, and for Trump. The legislation faced complications from Trump's proposed "anti-weaponization" fund, which would provide financial settlements to Trump allies. Shortly before passage, lawmakers rejected a Democratic amendment that would have blocked payments to anyone convicted of assaulting police during the January 6 Capitol riot.

The spending bill was also delayed by controversy over a proposed $1 billion allocation for security improvements at a ballroom Trump is constructing at the White House. Senate Republicans ultimately removed those funds after the chamber's parliamentarian ruled they could not be included while using budget reconciliation procedures to bypass the Democratic filibuster.

cards.headline: Trump administration cancels teen pregnancy prevention grants
cards.teaser: The Department of Health and Human Services canceled tens of millions of dollars in teen pregnancy prevention grants, prompting Democrats to demand reinstatement.
cards.body:
Democrats in both the House and Senate are demanding the Trump administration restore teen pregnancy prevention grants that were abruptly canceled last week. The Department of Health and Human Services terminated the funding without notifying program recipients in advance.

In the House, 79 Democrats led by members of the Democratic Women's Caucus sent a letter to Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy calling for reinstatement of the grants. The canceled funding had supported programs nationwide aimed at reducing teen pregnancy rates.

cards.headline: Appeals court blocks order to restore National Park Service signs
cards.teaser: A federal appeals court halted a lower court ruling that would have required the National Park Service to restore exhibits removed by the Trump administration.
cards.body:
The 1st Circuit Court of Appeals reversed a district court's requirement that the National Park Service restore signs and exhibits removed during the Trump administration. The appeals court decision allows the removals to continue while the case proceeds through the legal system.

Critics argue the administration is rewriting history by removing park materials from federal sites. The removals have affected historical narratives at locations including Mammoth Cave National Park, where exhibits documented the experiences of enslaved workers who contributed to early exploration and development of the site.

cards.headline: Trump declares National Scallops Day, criticizes predecessors
cards.teaser: President Trump announced a National Scallops Day to mark the opening of New England waters for scallop fishing while taking aim at former Presidents Obama and Biden.
cards.body:
President Trump declared a National Scallops Day to celebrate the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration opening New England waters for scallop fishing. The announcement came as the administration highlighted its approach to fishing regulations in the region.

Trump used the declaration to criticize former Presidents Obama and Biden, though he did not specify what policies he opposed. The move represents the administration's effort to showcase regulatory changes affecting the commercial fishing industry.

cards.headline: Former Olympic canoeist indicted over Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool damage
cards.teaser: A grand jury charged former Olympian David Hearn with felony property destruction in connection with damage at the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool.
cards.body:
A Washington grand jury has indicted David Hearn, a 67-year-old former Olympic canoeist, on a felony charge of property destruction. According to U.S. Attorney Jeanine Pirro, Hearn allegedly forcefully and violently pulled up and removed the bottom liner of the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool.

The incident occurred following a $14 million renovation of the landmark championed by President Trump. Hearn faces up to 10 years in prison if convicted of the felony charge.

cards.headline: US death rate reaches record low in 2025
cards.teaser: The death rate in the United States fell to its lowest level ever recorded, according to provisional CDC data released Thursday.
cards.body:
The death rate in the United States reached a historic low of 689.2 per 100,000 people in 2025, according to provisional data from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. This represents a 4.6 percent improvement compared to 2024.

The figures reflect an ongoing positive trend in American mortality rates. The CDC released these preliminary statistics through its Vital Statistics Rapid Release report as part of its regular monitoring of vital data across the country.

cards.headline: Top Army general in Europe and Africa steps down after ouster
cards.teaser: Army Gen. Christopher Donahue relinquished command in Germany after Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth unexpectedly removed him from the position last month.
cards.body:
Army Gen. Christopher Donahue formally relinquished command of U.S. Army Europe and Africa at a ceremony in Wiesbaden, Germany. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth removed Donahue from the position last month in a move that surprised military observers.

Donahue, 56, spent decades in military special operations and was considered a rising star in the Army. His removal by Hegseth was unexpected given his reputation and career trajectory within the service.
